content.text: All responsive locations inspected (§§ 1, 13, 14, 15, plus 10–12, 16, 24, 25 for hidden grants). The bargain is customer-favourable throughout, so I will submit a compliant finding without a redline.

input.quote: 14.2 Upon creation and subject to payment of the applicable Fees, Customer owns each Deliverable created specifically for Customer. Vendor hereby assigns to Customer all worldwide right, title, and interest in those Deliverables and shall obtain equivalent assignments from its personnel. Vendor will execute further documents reasonably needed to confirm ownership.
input.rationale: The IP package meets our preferred position, not merely the fallback. § 14.2 gives us ownership of each Deliverable on creation (subject to payment) with an express present assignment from Vendor plus personnel assignments and further-assurance cooperation; "Deliverable" (§ 1.4) captures reports, configurations, integrations, designs, workflows and other work product created specifically for us. § 14.3 lets Vendor retain only Vendor Technology, defined in § 1.9 as its pre-existing software, tools, models and templates (expressly excluding Customer Data and IP we owned before the Effective Date, i.e. generic tools and know-how only), and routes any embedded Vendor Technology to the § 13.2 licence, which is "perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free, fully paid" with rights to use, modify, create derivative works and have contractors support the material for our business. § 14.1 confirms we own all Customer Data, Customer Confidential Information and our independent IP, with only a limited processing right to Vendor, reinforced by § 15.1 (no sale, advertising, commingling or model training without our written consent) and § 10.1 (rights in accepted Deliverables, paid-up licences and Customer Data continue after termination). § 14.4 negates joint ownership absent a separate signed instrument that identifies exploitation rights, and keeps feedback voluntary with our unrestricted right to use our own feedback. There is no assignment of our IP or data to Vendor anywhere in the document. Two points are worth noting but are not deviations: § 13.3 permits suspension/revocation of a licence during a material uncured payment or use breach affecting the licensed item after notice and a cure opportunity, a customary qualification on irrevocability; and the Customer Data definition carves out anonymized operational telemetry that cannot be linked to us or an individual. Neither is material, so no redline.
